newsitem.title: UK: BOE TO ADAPT MONEY MKT OPERATIONS SHORT-TERM.
newsitem.headline: BOE TO ADAPT MONEY MKT OPERATIONS SHORT-TERM.

text.p: The Bank of England said on Wednesday it would adapt its money market operations for a couple of weeks starting Thursday, to smooth the redemption of a large Treasury loan.
Some of the 5.5 billion stg 8-3/4 percent Treasury loan due 1997 will be redeemed on September 1 and will generate a large cash flow to the market from that date.
"To offset this, and thus smooth the future pattern of daily shortages/surpluses, the Bank will make two adaptations to its money market operations from tomorrow," a Bank statement said.
On appropriate days, to be announced each morning, the Bank may include invitations of repo to September 1 in daily operations, in addition to its normal repo invitations.

Secondly, from August 14-20, the Bank will include holdings of the 1997 loan stock in the instruments it is prepared to buy outright in its daily operations. That will only apply at the 0845 GMT and 1100 GMT rounds each day.
